_comment: Issue #880 / ADR-0880. Each series is a run of dated notes asserting ONE fact (series.fact) through the same-fact key (group, source, target, name). Note n of a series is dated start + (n-1) days at 09:00:00Z, gets chunk_id '<fact>-<series>-<nn>' (plus '-c<k>' when chunks_per_note > 1; first_asserted is compared at note granularity, since chunks of one note tie and the uuid tie-break between them is arbitrary), and its text is '<fact> uses <fact>-target: <series> note <n>' unless fact_text is set (then verbatim). source_key travels in the episode `attributes` JSON until a dedicated column exists (ADR-0880 Follow-up). doc: 'per_note' gives each note its own doc_id ('doc-<fact>-<series>-<nn>'); 'none' supplies no doc_id, so every episode counts as its own document today. `expected` is what ADR-0880 specifies; `baseline_corroboration` is what the CURRENT counting rule reports and is asserted against the live service.

series.fact_text: J uses J-target: carried forward verbatim
J uses J-target: carried forward verbatim
J uses J-target: same thing, reworded

A.case: single author restates across 12 dated daily notes

C.case: alice x10 restates, bob confirms once: two sources, not 11

D.case: no source_key (legacy): identical to today, no backfill

E.case: one keyed note split into 3 chunks with no doc_id

F.case: keyed first note then 2 keyless notes: keyless notes each stay their own source

G.case: first assertion superseded: the next-earliest live restatement is promoted

H.case: external x3 from one site plus a primary author: units are origin-namespaced

I.case: derived page citing alice never forms a unit

J.case: verbatim copy and a rephrase by the same author are one unit

K.case: standup recap sharing its source note's key adds 0 independent support (retrieval-quality gain-1 near-duplicate)
